facts.value: Equines are a group of mammals that belong to the family Equidae.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Equines are known for their slender legs, hooves, and long faces with large, expressive eyes.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Equines are herbivores, feeding primarily on grasses and other vegetation.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: The origin of equines can be traced back to the Eocene epoch, which began about 56 million years ago.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: The first ancestral horses, known as Hyracotherium or Eohippus, appeared in what is now North America.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: These early equids were small, about the size of a small dog.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: They had four toes on their front feet and three toes on their hind feet.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Over millions of years, the equids gradually evolved into larger and more specialized forms.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: One of the most significant changes was the development of a single hoof on each foot, which allowed them to run faster and with greater endurance.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: By the end of the Miocene epoch, about 5 million years ago, equids had spread to other continents, including Asia and Europe.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Today, there are several species of equines, including horses, donkeys, and zebras.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: They have all evolved to fill different ecological niches and serve different purposes in human societies.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: They are not only valued for their physical abilities but also for their intelligence and social nature, making them integral to various human cultures.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick
